hints: Focus on what type of intermolecular force alkanes can have, since they are non-polar molecules with only C and H.
Count the electrons as you go from $\text{CH}_4$ to $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$, the total number keeps increasing with chain length.
Link more electrons to more easily induced temporary dipoles, which means stronger London dispersion forces and a higher boiling point.
walkthrough:
**Identify the forces present**

Alkanes are non-polar, simple molecular substances. The only intermolecular forces between their molecules are London dispersion forces, a type of van der Waals forces.

No permanent dipoles, no hydrogen bonding here.

**See what changes down the series**

From methane to butane the chain gets longer. The molecule gets larger and contains more electrons.

$\text{CH}_4$ (10 electrons) $\rightarrow$ $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ (18 electrons) $\rightarrow$ $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$ (26 electrons) $\rightarrow$ $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$ (34 electrons)

**Link electrons to boiling point**

More electrons means a larger, more polarisable electron cloud. Stronger temporary dipoles can form, so London dispersion forces get stronger.

Stronger intermolecular forces need more energy to separate, so boiling point rises: 112 K to 273 K.

options.A: Packing does affect van der Waals forces for branched isomers, but this trend is for straight chain length increasing. The key change here is molecular size and electron number, not closer packing. In fact longer chains have larger surface area for contact.
options.B: Boiling does not break covalent C-C or C-H bonds. It only overcomes weak intermolecular London dispersion forces between molecules. This is a very common trap, confusing intramolecular and intermolecular forces.
options.C: Correct. More electrons gives greater polarisability and stronger temporary dipole-induced dipole (London dispersion) forces. More energy is needed to separate the molecules, so boiling point increases from methane to butane.
options.D: Alkanes cannot form hydrogen bonds. Hydrogen bonding needs H attached to N, O or F, plus a lone pair on N, O or F. The H atoms in $\text{CH}_4$ to $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$ are all bonded to carbon only.
